# 3D printing conventions

## Semantic:
- Prefer one feature doing two jobs over two features (e.g. an opening that is both a port and a vent).

## Technical:
- Function comes first: a part must work, even if its look suffers. Within that, follow the project's artistic direction, and refine visible surfaces with chamfered edges and rounded parts.
- Design parts to print without supports: 45-degree slopes, gussets and pointed (V-shaped) openings instead of flat bridges and floating features.
- Inside a part, pointed (V-shaped) arches are fine. Openings visible from the outside (vents, slots, ports) get rounded ends where they are narrow enough (≈ 2 mm) to print without supports, and chamfered or pointed ends only where they are not.
- Strengthen a weak part underneath (overlaps where parts meet, fillets, thicker walls) rather than reshape it.
- Print the mounts for optional parts from the start, so they can be added later without a reprint.
- Printed models carry a maker's mark on the inside, naming the maker and the model. Ask the Maintainer for the names, and never remove an existing mark.
